fields.h1: Build an Advertorial Landing Page That Reads Like an Article
fields.hero_description: Build an advertorial landing page with an Advertisement label, tagged buy buttons, and each click saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an Advertorial
fields.features_subheading: From one description of the product and its reader, Emergent writes the article, its buttons, and the table that counts their clicks.
fields.feature_1:
An article drafted from your notes

Paste the founder's notes or a product brief, and Emergent drafts the page as an article: a headline, a byline, short paragraphs, and spots for photos. Ask for any change by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A label set above the headline

Write the label once, such as Advertisement or Paid Advertisement, and ask for it above the headline in the byline's type. Every headline version of the page carries the same label.
fields.feature_3:
A tag on every buy button

Name each button by its spot in the story, such as intro or end. Each click is saved as a row in a database you own, with the tag, the time, and the headline version it came from.
fields.feature_4:
Headline versions with their own links

Ask for a second headline, and Emergent builds it as a version of the same page with its own link for a second ad. The table counts visitors and clicks for each version.
fields.feature_5:
A form at the end, an email to the rep

End the article with a short form in place of a buy button. Each request lands in your table, and the app emails the person you name when an answer matches a rule you set.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Paid plans include full code export of the page and its table to your GitHub repository. Or publish on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Under the Advertisement label, three buttons that count

Hushmoor's founder tested six weighted blankets before she made her own, and the advertorial tells that story under an Advertisement label. Three buy buttons in the article are tagged intro, middle, and end. Last week they sent 1,240 readers to the shop: 690 from the end button, 380 from the middle, and 170 from the intro.
fields.tab_content_2:
By reason, the cost per meal drew the most clicks

Pebblefoot lists seven reasons dog owners switch to fresh food, and each reason ends with a link tagged with its number. Reason 4 sets the cost per meal next to kibble. It drew 342 of the month's 900 clicks to the shop, more than any other reason on the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two headlines, 2,000 visitors each

Dellwyn Filters wrote two headlines for one advertorial and gave each ad its own version of the page. One asks whether your tap water is safe; the other has a plumber explain what your filter misses. After 2,000 visitors each, the plumber's version sent 264 readers to the shop and the safety question sent 180.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every order of 8 windows or more goes to Ilse Navarro

Glasswick Windows tells how neighbors on Alder Street replaced drafty windows, and the article ends in a quote form asking for a ZIP code, the number of windows, and an email. When a request is for 8 windows or more, the app emails Ilse Navarro, the sales rep. That was 21 of last week's 58 requests.

faq_plan.q: What is an advertorial landing page?
How do I create an advertorial landing page?

plan.angle: Searchers for an advertorial landing page are paid-social and native-ad marketers who want to see what one looks like and get one live: the results are template galleries, a glossary definition and example roundups that stop at screenshots. This page shows four advertorials built from a prompt and what each one records: a founder story with three tagged buttons, a listicle that counts clicks by reason, two headline versions split by ad, and a lead-gen article that ends in a quote form whose bigger requests go to one rep. It also covers the part the roundups skip: the Advertisement label above the headline, placed where the FTC's native advertising guide asks.
tab_stories: Hushmoor's founder tells how she tested six weighted blankets before making her own, under an Advertisement label, and the three tagged buy buttons sent 1,240 readers to the shop last week: 690 from the end button, 380 from the middle and 170 from the intro.
Pebblefoot's listicle gives seven reasons dog owners switch to fresh food, each reason ends in a link tagged with its number, and reason 4, the cost per meal, drew 342 of the month's 900 clicks.

Dellwyn Filters runs two ads, each linked to its own headline version of one advertorial, and after 2,000 visitors each the plumber's headline sent 264 readers to the shop against 180 for the safety question.

Sunvale Solar's article about three neighbors who went solar ends in a 3-field quote form, and the app emails Ilse Navarro about every request with a monthly power bill of $150 or more: 21 of last week's 58.
